title: Fair Queue Eviction Consensus & Soft-Degrade Lanes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During multi-region incidents we observe tenant unfairness where requests from the same tenant are accepted in one region and evicted in another, leading to underutilized capacity and user-visible variability. Existing local eviction policies (token buckets + priority lanes) work well intra-region but lack a lightweight cross-region coordination layer. Goal: implement a low-latency, low-complexity consensus-lite mechanism to make eviction decisions 'fair' across regions while preserving SLO isolation and fast failover. Scope: design and implement 'Fair Eviction Consensus' that operates at the admission layer and a new set of soft-degrade lanes that provide bounded service-quality reduction instead of hard drops for medium-priority tenants.

Proposal summary: introduce an ephemeral per-tenant 'fairness score' that is periodically aggregated across regions (every 3s) using a gossip-assisted lightweight vector (hash+counter) instead of strict consensus. Admissions consult this score to bias eviction probability: tenants with historical lower acceptance get priority. Soft-degrade lanes implement graceful response transformations (token trimming, heuristics-based early-stop, compressed-logging) to keep requests accepted but cheaper. We will keep the mechanism opt-in per-tenant and default to current local behavior unless enabled via rollout flags.

Design decisions and trade-offs: - Consistency vs latency: we avoid strong distributed locks or leader elections to prevent added tail latency. Gossip window provides eventual alignment with bounded staleness (3s target). - Complexity vs observability: add small metadata (4 bytes) to per-request admission path to carry last-known fairness token; increases request metadata but simplifies debugging. - Fairness granularity: use tenant-level grouping (by account id) to avoid per-user state explosion. For high-cardinality customers we bucket by tenant-shard. - SLO alignment: admission bias only applied when local admission is active (queue occupancy > threshold). Under normal load path behavior unchanged.

API and config surface: - new runtime config area: fairness.enabled (boolean), fairness.window_secs (int), fairness.bias_alpha (float 0..1) - admission call signature: admit(request, ctx) -> {decision, trace_reason, fairness_token} - rollout flags per-workspace and per-routing policy (console + env)

Metrics and SLOs (observable): - fairness.sync_lag_seconds (gauge) - per-tenant accept_rate_by_region (counter) - eviction_bias_applied (counter, labels: tenant, region) - soft_degrade_activation (counter) - p99/p95 tail latency before/after bias (dashboard) SLO considerations: ensure 99th percentile latency remains within 1.1x baseline when fairness.enabled=false; when enabled, target SLO for affected tenants: availability drop capped at 5% with documented degradation modes.

Testing and validation: - unit tests for token merge rules and bias math - local integration harness to run multi-region admission simulator (replay production traces with region skew) - staging canary on 10% tenants with gradual ramp and synthetic traffic spikes - chaos test: inject region partition and verify no double-evictions and bounded sync_lag

Rollout plan: 1) Merge core algorithm + feature flags behind internal config 2) Canary (internal tenants) for 48h with telemetry checks 3) Pilot with opt-in external customer (one high-traffic tenant) 4) 10% global ramp with aggressive monitoring 5) 100% opt-in enable by tenant UI; global default remains off

Operational runbook (short): - If eviction variance > 15% across regions, enable debug logging flag and inspect fairness.sync_lag_seconds and per-tenant accept_rate_by_region dashboards. - If sync_lag > 10s, temporarily disable fairness for affected regions by toggling fairness.window_secs or fairness.enabled. - For incidents where soft-degrade causes unacceptable correctness regressions, revert soft_degrade.enabled for tenant and open follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Fairness token propagated and merged without adding >2ms median admission latency
Unit + integration tests covering merge semantics and bias math pass
Canary telemetry shows <5% availability delta for pilot tenants and p99 latency <1.2x baseline
Operator dashboards for fairness.sync_lag_seconds, eviction_bias_applied, and soft_degrade_activation are created and documented
Rollout document, feature flag controls, and tenant opt-in UI hooks exist
notes: This is intentionally conservative: fairness only influences probabilistic eviction decisions, not hard quarantines.
Consider follow-up to expose per-tenant historical windows for billing reconciliation if acceptance variance affects SLAs.
We may reuse the gossip layer being prototyped in ENG-913579 for faster alignment once that lands.
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting — aligned on 'gossip token' vs 'leader election'. Action: prototype merge function (Asha).

2026-03-03: Design review with runtime and infra. Concern from infra: additional metadata on requests increases egress for cross-region; quantified as ~0.5% bandwidth. Decision: compress token to 32-bit hash; keep window at 3s. (Marco)
2026-03-04: Implementation started. Added token merge util and simulated admission bias routine in local harness. Early perf: +1.3ms median admission in the prototype. (Dev note)
2026-03-05: PM review (Riley Chen) — suggested adding opt-in flags per-tenant and console toggle. Created PM follow-up: PM-2148 to add console controls.

2026-03-07: Security review request opened (sec-req-421). No blocking crypto concerns; tokens are non-identifying hashes. Security asked for audit log hooks for when fairness changes; added to acceptance criteria. (Marco)

2026-03-08: Integration test failed under synthetic spike: soft-degrade lane produced truncated outputs that broke internal downstream checker. Mitigation: adjust degrade heuristic to preserve required tokens and add integration test for downstream contract. Creating follow-up ENG-981235. (Asha)
2026-03-09: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4829 — ongoing review. CI passing except intermittent flakiness in gossip convergence test; infra investigating. (link to PR)
2026-03-10: Updated rollout plan after ops feedback: add staging canary for 72h and create alert if per-tenant accept-rate deviates >10% across regions. (Marco)
